In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Tin

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinai﴾ ﴿and this secure city﴾.

At-tin (the fig) is the well-known fruit which has no pit (ajam) and no skin. Az-zaytun (the olive) is likewise the fruit from which oil is extracted. ﴿Tur Sinin﴾ is the Mount of Tur upon which Musa (Moses) conversed with his Lord. Al-balad al-amin is Makkah al-Mukarramah (the Honored). The waw is for oath.

Scholars have differed about what is meant by the first two things sworn by, at-tin and az-zaytun, while they agreed about the third and fourth, as will come.

As for at-tin and az-zaytun: from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, it is related that they are the two well-known fruits. This is also the view of 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Mujahid. They all say: at-tin is your fig which you eat, and az-zaytun is your olive which you press.

From Ka'b: at-tin is the Masjid of Damascus, and az-zaytun is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Likewise from Qatadah. They meant the places where the fig and olive grow, by the indication of Tur and the secure city, so that the growing place of the fig and olive is for 'Isa (Jesus), Tur Sinin is for Musa, and the secure city is for Muhammad ﷺ.

However, taking at-tin and az-zaytun to mean their places of growth has no evidence, so it is better to leave them on their original meaning. The following supports this:

First, at-tin: they said it is the most similar of fruits to the fruit of Paradise, since it has no pit and no skin. And there came concerning it in the Sunnah: "The Prophet ﷺ was presented with a tray containing figs. He ate from it, then said to his companions: 'If I were to say that a fruit had descended from Paradise, I would say this one; for the fruit of Paradise has no pit. So eat it, for it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout.'" Al-Naysaburi mentioned it and did not mention who narrated it.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned it in Zad al-Ma'ad, saying: "It is mentioned from Abu al-Darda', 'A tray of figs was presented to (p-4) the Prophet ﷺ,'" and he cited the text mentioned above. Then he said: "On the authenticity of this there is room for doubt."

The commentators, Ibn al-Qayyim and the author of al-Qamus, have mentioned that figs have properties, and they said: it is among the things that make it a fitting object of oath. Ibn al-Qayyim affirmed that it is the intended meaning in the surah.

Among the properties they mentioned, they said: it clears sand from the kidneys and bladder, protects from poisons, benefits roughness of the throat, chest and windpipe, cleanses the liver and spleen, purges phlegmatic humour from the stomach, nourishes the body with good nourishment, and its dried form nourishes and benefits the nerves.

Galen said: when eaten with walnuts and sadhab (rue), before taking a deadly poison, it benefits and protects from harm; it benefits chronic coughing, promotes urination, and quenches thirst arising from salty phlegm; and eating it on an empty stomach has a wondrous benefit.

Ibn al-Qayyim said: since it does not grow in the land of Hijaz and Madinah, no mention of it came in the Sunnah; but Allah has sworn by it in His Book, because of the abundance of its benefits and advantages.

The correct view is that the thing sworn by is the well-known fig. End of quote.

As Ibn al-Qayyim said: it is not mentioned in the Sunnah because it does not exist in Hijaz and Madinah. Likewise, its mention does not occur in the Qur'an at all except in this place. It did not grow in the places of Hijaz and Madinah because its climate is incompatible with their climate; and although it has been found there recently, it does not thrive there as it does elsewhere.

Thus it is preponderant that the intended at-tin is this eaten fruit, as came from those we named: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan.

As for az-zaytun: the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already stated in the introduction that among the kinds of clarification is this: when there is disagreement about the intended meaning, and the appearance of one of the two meanings, or of the several probable meanings, is more frequent in the Qur'an, then it is more appropriate to interpret the word according to it.

The mention of az-zaytun has come in the Qur'an several times, intending by it that blessed tree. It is mentioned among trees in particular in His saying in Surat al-An'am: ﴿and gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-An'am: 99]. He named it by itself in His saying in Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿and a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai, producing oil and a condiment for those who eat﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 20] (p-5) He mentioned it along with the date palm and grain in 'Abasa in His saying: ﴿then We caused grain to grow therein﴾ ﴿and grapes and herbage﴾ ﴿and olives and palm trees﴾ [‘Abasa: 27–29]. And He mentioned one of the most distinctive properties of trees in His saying in Surat an-Nur, in the great parable: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp within a glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star lit from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light﴾ [an-Nur: 35]. So He described it with blessing, and described its oil as almost giving light even if no fire touched it. And its being chosen for this great parable makes it fit for this great oath here.

As for Tur Sinin: most of them hold that it is the Mount of Tur, upon which Allah spoke to Musa, as came in several places. Its mention there is for honor and for oath. From its mention for honor is His saying: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mount﴾ [Maryam: 52]. From its mention for oath is His saying: ﴿By the Mount﴾ ﴿and a written Book﴾ [at-Tur: 1–2].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already stated his view in Surat at-Tur, and Allah swore by the Mount in His saying: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinai﴾ [at-Tin: 2]. End of quote.

As for al-balad al-amin, it is Makkah, based on His saying: ﴿and whoever enters it is safe﴾. So al-amin here means al-amin in the sense of safe (al-amin), i.e., from enemies, that they would fight its people or raid them, as He said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67]. And al-amin in the sense of safe (amin) came in the poet's verse:

Did you not know, O Ism, woe to you, that I swore an oath that I would not betray my trusted one?

He means: my safe one.

[p. 456]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Tin (The Fig)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this secure city.﴾

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

The way of reconciling this verse with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾ [90] has already been explained.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾.

﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ (Indeed, We created man in the best of stature).

وَهَذا هو المُقْسَمُ عَلَيْهِ، والتَّقْوِيمُ التَّعْدِيلُ كَما في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجا﴾ ﴿قَيِّمًا﴾ [الكهف: ١ - ٢]، وأحْسَنُ تَقْوِيمٍ شامِلٌ لِخَلْقِ الإنْسانِ حِسًّا ومَعْنًى أيْ شَكْلًا وصُورَةً وإنْسانِيَّةً، وكُلُّها مِن آياتِ القُدْرَةِ ودَلالَةِ البَعْثِ.

This is the thing sworn to. Taqwim means ta'dil (proportioning), as in His words: ﴿He has not made in it any crookedness﴾ ﴿but made it straight﴾ [al-Kahf: 1-2]. "The best stature" includes the creation of man both sensibly and in meaning, that is, in form, shape and humanity, and all of these are among the signs of power and evidence of the Resurrection.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ:

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him:

؎دَواؤُكَ مِنكَ ولا تَشْعُرُ وداؤُكَ مِنكَ ولا تُبْصِرُ

Your cure is from you, yet you do not perceive it, and your disease is from you, yet you do not see it.

؎(p-٦)وَتَزْعُمُ أنَّكَ جِرْمٌ صَغِيرُ ∗∗∗ وفِيكَ انْطَوى العالَمُ الكَبِيرُ

[p. 6] You suppose that you are a small body, while within you the great world is folded up.

وَقَدْ بَيَّنَ تَعالى خَلْقَهُ ابْتِداءً مِن نُطْفَةٍ فَعَلَقَةٍ إلى آخِرِهِ في أكْثَرَ مِن مَوْضِعٍ، كَما في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ألَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِن مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوّى﴾ ﴿فَجَعَلَ مِنهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثى﴾ ﴿ألَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى﴾ [القيامة: ٣٤ - ٤٠].

Allah has explained His creation of man, beginning from a drop (nutfah), then a clinging clot (alaqah), and so on to its end, in more than one place, as in His words: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned﴾ ﴿and made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾ ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37-40].

وَكَذَلِكَ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ التَّنْبِيهُ عَلى البَعْثِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ [التين: ٧].

Likewise, in this surah there is an alert to the Resurrection in His words: ﴿So what causes you still to deny the Judgment?﴾ [al-Tin: 7].

أمّا الجانِبُ المَعْنَوِيُّ فَهو الجانِبُ الإنْسانِيُّ، وهو المُتَقَدِّمُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَنَفْسٍ وما سَوّاها﴾ عَلى ما قَدَّمْنا هُناكَ، مِن أنَّ النَّفْسَ البَشَرِيَّةَ هي مَناطُ التَّكْلِيفِ، وهو الجانِبُ الَّذِي بِهِ كانَ الإنْسانُ إنْسانًا، وبِهِما كانَ خَلْقُهُ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ، ونالَ بِذَلِكَ أعْلى دَرَجاتِ التَّكْرِيمِ: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾ [الإسراء: ٧٠].

As for the non-physical aspect, it is the human aspect, which was mentioned earlier in His words: ﴿and a soul and He who proportioned it﴾, as we have already set out there, that the human soul is the basis of moral responsibility. It is the aspect by which man is man, and by both of these his creation was in the best of stature, and by this he attained the highest degrees of honour: ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾ [al-Isra': 70].

وَالإنْسانُ وإنْ كانَ لَفْظًا مُفْرَدًا إلّا أنَّهُ لِلْجِنْسِ بِدَلالَةِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْناهُ أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ﴾ ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [التين: ٥ - ٦]، وهَذا مِثْلُ ما في سُورَةِ: ﴿والعَصْرِ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ﴾ ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وتَواصَوْا بِالحَقِّ وتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ [العصر: ١ - ٦]، فَبِاسْتِثْناءِ الجَمْعِ مِنهُ، عُلِمَ أنَّ المُرادَ بِهِ الجِنْسُ.

Although al-insan is singular in form, it refers to the genus, as shown by His words: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ ﴿except for those who believe﴾ [al-Tin: 5-6]. This is like what is in the surah: ﴿By time﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 1-3]. By excepting the plural from it, it is known that what is meant by it is the genus.

وَالتَّأْكِيدُ بِالقَسَمِ المُتَقَدِّمِ عَلى خَلْقِ الإنْسانِ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ يُشْعِرُ أنَّ المُخاطَبَ مُنْكِرٌ لِذَلِكَ، مَعَ أنَّ هَذا أمْرٌ مَلْمُوسٌ مَحْسُوسٌ، لا يُنْكِرُهُ إنْسانٌ.

The emphasis by the oath preceding the creation of man in the best of stature indicates that the addressee denies this, even though this is a tangible, perceptible matter that no human being denies.

وَقَدْ أجابَ الشَّيْخُ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ تَعالى عَلَيْنا وعَلَيْهِ في دَفْعِ إيهامِ الِاضْطِرابِ عَلى ذَلِكَ: بِأنَّ غَيْرَ المُنْكِرِ إذا ظَهَرَتْ عَلَيْهِ عَلاماتُ الإنْكارِ، عُومِلَ مُعامَلَةَ المُنْكِرِ، كَقَوْلِ الشّاعِرِ:

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and him, answered in removing the appearance of inconsistency concerning this: that one who is not a denier, when signs of denial appear upon him, is treated as a denier, like the words of the poet:

؎جاءَ شَقِيقٌ عارِضًا رُمْحَهُ ∗∗∗ وإنَّ بَنِي عَمِّكَ فِيهِمْ رِماحُ

Shaqiq came displaying his spear, and indeed the sons of your paternal uncle have spears among them.

وَأماراتُ الإنْكارِ عَلى المُخاطَبِينَ، إنَّما هي عَدَمُ إيمانِهِمْ بِالبَعْثِ؛ لِأنَّ العاقِلَ لَوْ تَأمَّلَ خَلْقَ الإنْسانِ، لَعَرَفَ مِنهُ أنَّ القادِرَ عَلى خَلْقِهِ في هَذِهِ الصُّورَةِ، قادِرٌ عَلى بَعْثِهِ.

The signs of denial in the addressees are only their not believing in the Resurrection, because if the intelligent person reflected on the creation of man, he would know from it that the One able to create him in this form is able to resurrect him.

وَهَذِهِ المَسْألَةُ أفْرَدَها الشَّيْخُ في سُورَةِ الجاثِيَةِ بِتَنْبِيهٍ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكم وما يَبُثُّ مِن دابَّةٍ آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ [الجاثية: ٤]، وتَكَرَّرَ هَذا البَحْثُ في عِدَّةِ مَواضِعَ، وأصْرَحُ دَلالَةٍ عَلى هَذا المَعْنى ما جاءَ في آخِرِ يس: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلًا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قالَ مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وهو بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [يس: ٧٨ - ٧٩].

The Shaykh dealt with this question separately in the commentary on surah al-Jathiyah, by drawing attention to His words: ﴿And in your creation and in what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for a people who are certain﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4]. This discussion recurs in several places, and the clearest indication of this meaning is what comes at the end of Ya-Sin: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78-79].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

قال المؤلف في (دفع إيهام الإضطراب عن آيات الكتاب):

The author said in (Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book):

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ .

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾.

هَذِهِ الآيَةُ الكَرِيمَةُ تُوهِمُ أنَّ الإنْسانَ يُنْكِرُ أنَّ رَبَّهُ خَلَقَهُ، لِما تَقَرَّرَ في فَنِّ المَعانِي مِن أنَّ خالِيَ الذِّهْنِ مِنَ المُتَرَدِّدِ، والإنْكارُ لا يُؤَكَّدُ لَهُ الكَلامُ، ويُسَمّى ذَلِكَ ابْتِدائِيًّا، والمُتَرَدِّدُ يَحْسُنُ التَّوْكِيدُ لَهُ بِمُؤَكِّدٍ واحِدٍ، ويُسَمّى طَلَبِيًّا، والمُنْكِرُ يَجِبُ التَّوْكِيدُ لَهُ بِحَسَبِ إنْكارِهِ، ويُسَمّى إنْكارِيًّا.

This noble verse gives the impression that man denies that his Lord created him, because it is established in the science of meanings (fann al-ma'ani, the branch of Arabic rhetoric concerned with meaning in context) that one whose mind is free of doubt is not to be given emphasis in speech; this is called ibtida'i (initial, unemphasized). One who is hesitant is well addressed with a single emphasis, and this is called talabi (requested). One who denies must be addressed with emphasis in proportion to his denial, and this is called inkari (denying).

وَاللَّهُ تَعالى في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ أكَّدَ إخْبارَهُ بِأنَّهُ خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ، بِأرْبَعَةِ أقْسامٍ، وبِاللّامِ، وبِقَدْ، فَهي سِتَّةُ تَأْكِيداتٍ، وهَذا التَّوْكِيدُ يُوهِمُ أنَّ الإنْسانَ مُنْكِرٌ، لِأنَّ رَبَّهُ خَلَقَهُ، وقَدْ جاءَتْ آياتٌ أُخْرى صَرِيحَةٌ في أنَّ الكُفّارَ يُقِرُّونَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ هو خالِقُهم، وهي قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَألْتَهم مَن خَلَقَهم لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ﴾ [الزخرف: ٨٧].

In this verse Allah emphasized His report that He created man in the best of stature with four oaths, with the lam, and with qad; these are six emphases. This emphasis gives the impression that man is a denier, since his Lord created him, and other verses clearly state that the disbelievers acknowledge that Allah is their Creator, namely His words: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87].

وَالجَوابُ مِن وجْهَيْنِ:

The answer is in two respects:

الأوَّلُ: هو ما حَرَّرَهُ عُلَماءُ البَلاغَةِ مِن أنَّ المُقِرَّ، إذا ظَهَرَتْ عَلَيْهِ أمارَةُ الإنْكارِ، جُعِلَ كالمُنْكِرِ، فَأُكِّدَ لَهُ الخَبَرُ، كَقَوْلِ حَجْلِ بْنِ نَضْلَةَ:

The first: it is what the scholars of rhetoric have clarified, that the one who acknowledges, when signs of denial appear upon him, is treated as a denier, so the statement is emphasized for him, like the words of Hajl ibn Nadlah:

؎جاءَ شَقِيقٌ عارِضًا رُمْحَهُ أنَّ بَنِي عَمِّكَ فِيهِمْ رِماحْ

Shaqiq came displaying his spear; indeed the sons of your paternal uncle have spears among them.

فَشَقِيقٌ لا يُنْكِرُ أنَّ في بَنِي عَمِّهِ رِماحًا، ولَكِنَّ مَجِيئَهُ عارِضًا رُمْحَهُ، أيْ جاعِلًا عَرْضَهُ جِهَتَهم مِن غَيْرِ التِفاتِ إمارَةٍ، أنَّهُ يَعْتَقِدُ أنْ لا رُمْحَ فِيهِمْ، فَأكَّدَ لَهُ الخَبَرَ، فَإذا حَقَّقْتَ ذَلِكَ، فاعْلَمْ أنَّ الكُفّارَ لَمّا أنْكَرُوا البَعْثَ، ظَهَرَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أمارَةُ إنْكارِ الإيجادِ (p-٤٥٧)الأوَّلِ، لِأنَّ مَن أقَرَّ بِالأوَّلِ لَزِمَهُ الإقْرارُ بِالثّانِي، لِأنَّ الإعادَةَ أيْسَرُ مِنَ البَدْءِ، فَأكَّدَ لَهُمُ الإيجادَ الأوَّلَ.

Shaqiq does not deny that the sons of his paternal uncle have spears, but his coming displaying his spear, that is, turning its side towards them without any sign of looking, shows that he believes they have no spear, so the statement is emphasized for him. When you have verified this, know that when the disbelievers denied the Resurrection, signs of denial of the first creation [p. 457] appeared upon them, because whoever acknowledges the first creation is bound to acknowledge the second, since restoration is easier than initiation, so the first creation was emphasized for them.

وَيُوَضِّحُ هَذا أنَّ اللَّهَ بَيَّنَ أنَّهُ المَقْصُودُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ [التين: ٧]، أيْ ما يَحْمِلُكَ أيُّها الإنْسانُ عَلى التَّكْذِيبِ بِالبَعْثِ والجَزاءِ، بَعْدَ عِلْمِكَ أنَّ اللَّهَ أوْجَدَكَ أوَّلًا، فَمَن أوْجَدَكَ أوَّلًا قادِرٌ عَلى أنْ يُوجِدَكَ ثانِيًا، كَما قالَ تَعالى: ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ الآيَةَ [يس: ٧٩]، وقالَ: ﴿كَما بَدَأْنا أوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ﴾ الآيَةَ [الأنبياء: ١٠٤]، وقالَ: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ الآيَةَ [الروم: ٢٧] وقالَ: ﴿ياأيُّها النّاسُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ في رَيْبٍ مِنَ البَعْثِ فَإنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن تُرابٍ﴾ [الحج: ٥].

This is made clear by the fact that Allah explained that what is meant by His words: ﴿So what causes you still to deny the Judgment?﴾ [al-Tin: 7] is: what leads you, O man, to deny the Resurrection and the recompense, after your knowledge that Allah originated you first? For whoever originated you first is able to originate you a second time, as He said: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time"﴾ — the verse [Ya-Sin: 79]; and He said: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ — the verse [al-Anbiya': 104]; and He said: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it﴾ — the verse [al-Rum: 27]; and He said: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed, We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

وَالآياتُ بِمِثْلِ هَذا كَثِيرَةٌ، ولِذا ذَكَرَ تَعالى أنَّ مَن أنْكَرَ البَعْثَ، فَقَدْ نَسِيَ إيجادَهُ الأوَّلَ، بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلًا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قالَ مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ [يس: ٧٨]، وبِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الإنْسانُ أئِذا ما مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا أوَلا يَذْكُرُ الإنْسانُ أنّا خَلَقْناهُ مِن قَبْلُ ولَمْ يَكُ شَيْئًا﴾ [مريم: ٦٦ - ٦٧].

Verses of this kind are numerous, and for this reason Allah mentioned that whoever denies the Resurrection has forgotten his first origination, in His words: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], and in His words: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?" Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?﴾ [Maryam: 66-67].

وَقالَ البَعْضُ: مَعْنى: ﴿فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ﴾، فَمَن يَقْدِرُ عَلى تَكْذِيبِكَ يا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ بِالثَّوابِ والعِقابِ بَعْدَما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أنّا خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ عَلى ما وصَفْنا، وهو في دَلالَتِهِ عَلى ما ذَكَرْنا كالأوَّلِ، فَظَهَرَتِ النُّكْتَةُ في جَعْلِ الِابْتِدائِيِّ كالإنْكارِيِّ.

Some have said: the meaning of ﴿So what causes you﴾ is: who can deny you, O Prophet of Allah, regarding reward and punishment, after it has become clear that We created man as We have described? And this, in its indication of what we have mentioned, is like the first. Thus the point is made clear in treating the initial (ibtida'i) as the denying (inkari).

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: أنَّ القَسَمَ شامِلٌ لِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْناهُ أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ﴾ [التين: ٥]، أيْ إلى النّارِ، وهم لا يُصَدِّقُونَ بِالنّارِ بِدَلِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿هَذِهِ النّارُ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ بِها تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ [الطور: ١٤].

The second: the oath includes His words: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 5], that is, to the Fire, and they do not believe in the Fire, as evidenced by His words: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [al-Tur: 14].

وَهَذا الوَجْهُ في مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ﴾ أصَحُّ مِنَ القَوْلِ بِأنَّ مَعْناهُ الهَرَمُ، والرَّدُّ إلى أرْذَلِ العُمُرِ لِكَوْنِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَلَهم أجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾ [التين: ٦] أظْهَرَ في الأوَّلِ مِنَ الثّانِي، وإذا كانَ القَسَمُ شامِلًا لِلْإنْكارِيِّ، فَلا إشْكالًا لِأنَّ التَّوْكِيدَ مُنْصَبٌّ عَلى ذَلِكَ الإنْكارِيِّ، والعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَعالى.

This view regarding the meaning of ﴿lowest of the low﴾ is more correct than the view that it means senility and being returned to the most abject age, because His words ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted﴾ [al-Tin: 6] are more apparent in the first than in the second. And if the oath includes the denying case, then there is no difficulty, because the emphasis is directed at that denying case. And Allah knows best.

(p-7)Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾.

It has been said: he is returned to old age, senility, and weakness of body and mind.

Eighty years, and I have reached them, have made my hearing in need of an interpreter.

This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 68].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, mentioned this view and cited along with it His saying: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair﴾ [al-Rum: 54]. He also cited this verse of al-Tin, ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, and said: "according to one of the two interpretations." He also cited His saying: ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he knows nothing after knowing﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. This meaning is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

It has also been said: he is returned to the Fire because of his disbelief. This is related from Mujahid and al-Hasan.

Ibn Jarir preferred the first meaning, and it is as you see, supported by the Qur'an in the texts we have presented. He also argued for this view from the same surah, because Allah the Exalted said at its end: ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment after this?﴾ [al-Tin: 7], meaning: after these clear proofs, namely the beginning of man's creation and his development to the best of his state, then his return to the lowest degrees of helplessness, "the lowest of the low." This is what they witness, and it is used as an argument against them.

As for his being returned to the Fire, it is something they have not witnessed and do not believe in, so it cannot serve as a proof that is established against them, because the nature of a proof is that it moves from the known to the unknown. The Resurrection is the very point of their denial, so one cannot argue against them to establish what they deny by means of what they deny. This which he has adopted is clear.

Among what supports this view is that man's condition in his formation is: from a drop, then a clinging clot, then a child, then a youth, then an old man, then a decrepit one, and weakness. A similar pattern appears in plants, and both are among the signs of the Resurrection, as in His saying: ﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿like a rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turning yellow, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and approval﴾ [al-Hadid: 20]. (p-8) And His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out by it crops of varying colors, then it dries up and you see it turning yellow, then He makes it debris? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 21].

Likewise is man, for he is like the plant, the same, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth like plants﴾ ﴿Then He returns you into it and brings you forth in a [definite] emergence﴾ [Nuh: 17-18].

The exception, "except those who believe," is then understood to mean that they do not reach the state of decrepitude and the lowest age, because the believer, however long his life, is in obedience and in the remembrance of Allah, so he has full intellect. It is well established among both the common people and the elite that the one who memorizes the Book of Allah and constantly recites it is not afflicted by senility or incoherent speech.

We have witnessed the shaykh of the reciters in Medina, the Shaykh Hasan al-Sha'ir, who, at the time of writing these lines, is still alive and has passed one hundred by a great deal. He still teaches the Qur'an to his students and instructs them in the ten readings, and he sometimes listens to more than one person reciting in more than one place while keeping track of all of them.

al-Shawkani also related something similar from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said this.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 95, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For them is a reward never cut off﴾.

That is: not cut off, or not bestowed upon them with reproach (ghayr mamnun bihi 'alayhim).

According to the first meaning: the reward is the recompense, either through the continuation of their deeds because of the perfection of their intellects, or because Allah commands the angels to record for them the reward of what they used to do in their time of strength, such as fasting, standing in prayer, and giving charity from their earnings, and the like, on the basis of the hadiths concerning the sick person and the traveller. Thus the recompense of their deeds continues for them, not cut off.

According to the second meaning: the reward is the bliss of Paradise, which is given to them and is not bestowed upon them with reproach, and is not cut off from them, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Its fruit is perpetual and its shade; that is the final outcome of those who were mindful of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35].

Note (tanbih)

Here there is a point of view from two angles: a particular angle and a general angle.

As for the particular: the word "radadnahu" (We returned him) implies a return to a prior state, and the prior state is the creation of man in the best of forms (ahsan taqwim). The best of forms encompasses his shape and his meaning, that is, his body and his humanity. So his return to the lowest of the low (asfal safilin) occurs through lack of faith, becoming like an animal; rather, in that state he is lower in rank than the animal and fiercer in soul than the beast, for no faith governs him and no humanity refines him, so he becomes a tyrannical oppressor who spreads corruption in the earth. Accordingly, the exception is ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: by their faith and their righteous deeds they rise above baseness and ascend to the heights, so ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾.

The general angle, which encompasses the subject of the surah from its beginning, starting with "By the fig and the olive" and what accompanies them in the oath, to: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾ ﴿then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ ﴿except those who believe﴾ and so on [al-Tin: 4-6].

For if what has come in the story of Adam is sound, in His saying: ﴿So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121], the exegetes narrated that when Adam's private parts became apparent to him, he went to the trees of the Garden to take leaves to cover himself, and whenever he came to a tree it rebuked him and did not give him any, until he passed by the fig tree, which gave him some. So Allah rewarded it by making its fruit yield twice a year, and recompensed it by making its inside like its outside, with no peel and no pit.

Al-Shawkani also narrated that it was the fig tree from which he took the leaves. He said: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When Allah made Adam dwell in the Garden, He clothed him with a garment of nails (al-zufr). When he committed the sin, He stripped him of the garment, and it remained on the tips of his fingers."

He said: al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The clothing of Adam and Eve was like the nail" — and he mentioned the report — ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾. He said: they would strip off the leaves of the fig tree and place them over their private parts.

By this narration, the mention of the fig here, together with "We created man in the best of stature, then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe," is a very subtle secret: it alerts man now that the whole human race is in the first man, the father of mankind, whom Allah created in the best state, physically and spiritually, to the point of raising him to the rank of the angels prostrating to him and his dwelling in the Garden, which is the highest rank of honour. In it, he would not hunger, nor go naked, nor thirst, nor be exposed to the sun, and he remained thus until Satan misled him and he forgot the covenant of his Lord to him, and fell into what he fell into, and what came to be came to be. So he lured them both with deception, and they moved from the highest of the high (a'la 'illiyyin) to the lowest of the low (asfal safilin). He descended to the earth, ploughing, sowing, reaping, grinding, kneading and baking, until he found the morsel of sustenance. This is the creation of man in the best of stature and his return to the lowest of the low.

This is the condition of the people of the earth all together, except those who believe and do righteous deeds: ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾, by their return to Paradise as Adam returned to it through repentance: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 37] ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾ [Ta-Ha: 122].

And in the mention of "this secure land" (al-balad al-amin) there is indeed a reinforcement of this meaning, because Allah made the sanctuary a security for the people of Makkah, like the image of the secure one in Paradise. If they comply and obey, they enjoy this security; but if they rebel and disobey, they will be expelled from it and deprived of its security.

Thus the surah becomes a link between the past and the present, and a launch from the present toward the future: ﴿So what causes you to deny the Recompense after [this]?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin: 7-8]. Concerning what He did with Adam, and what He does with those [who believe], to whom He bestowed security and comfortable living, and the sending of you to them, and concerning what He does for those who believe or for those who disbelieve. Indeed, yes.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 95, verse 7:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So what causes you to deny the Recompense after this?﴾

Ad-din (al-din, the recompense) is the requital, as in surah al-Fatihah: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]. The address is said to be to the Messenger ﷺ. And "ma" in His saying "fa-ma" is in the sense of "man," meaning: who is it that denies you after this clarification, with the coming of the recompense and the reckoning, so that each person may receive the reward of his deeds?

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾

The question is as has already been explained in ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1], meaning it is for affirmation. He, glory be to Him and exalted, is without doubt the most just of judges, as it has been confirmed from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when he recited it he would say: "Allahumma bala" ("O Allah, yes indeed"), as will come later.

As for "ahkam al-hakimin" (the most just of judges), it has been said that it is an "af'al al-tafdil" (the comparative/superlative form) from "hukm" (judgment), meaning the most just of judges, as in the Almighty's saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

It has also been said that it derives from "hikmah" (wisdom), meaning in His craftsmanship, perfection and creation. In that case the word is "mushtarak" (a homonym, having more than one meaning), and it is not far-fetched that it may carry both meanings together, although the meaning of judgment is more apparent, because the "hakim" (wise one) derived from "hikmah" is pluralized as "hukama'" (the wise).

Based on the view that both meanings are intended, this is the use of the homonym in both its meanings simultaneously. Here there is no contradiction; rather, the two are mutually entailed, because the one who is wise must be just, and the one who is just must be wise, placing matters in their proper places.

The Almighty has clarified this meaning in several places, such as His saying: ﴿Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds the same as the corruptors on earth? Or shall We treat the God-fearing the same as the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28], the answer being: No. And His saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them the same as those who believe and do righteous deeds, that their living and their dying would be equal? How evil is their judgment!﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21]. In His saying ﴿How evil is their judgment!﴾ there is an explanation of their lack of justice in judgment and their distance from wisdom.

It is known that the non-equality between them in death is due to resurrection and recompense. So He, glory be to Him, is the most just of judges in His craftsmanship and creation. He created man in the best form, and the most just of judges in His judgment does not treat the good-doer and the evildoer alike.

The exegetes have agreed upon the narration of al-Tirmidhi concerning the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ and then recites ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, let him say: 'Bala (yes indeed), and I am among the witnesses to that.'"

A similar report comes from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: "Subhanaka Allahumma, fa-bala" ("Glory be to You, O Allah, so yes indeed"). And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.
